html: Colds come from many different viruses that settle in the nose and throat. Most people feel better within a week to ten days. Antibiotics don't help, because they don't work on viruses.

• A tickle or scratch in the throat on the first day
  • Congestion and a runny nose
  • A cough that can linger after everything else fades
  • Feeling tired or a little achy

• Rest and drink plenty of fluids
  • Warm drinks or a saltwater gargle can soothe a sore throat
  • Wash your hands and use tissues to protect the people around you

image.alt: Illustration of hands being washed under running water
image.caption: Soap, water and a good scrub keep germs from spreading.
image.title: Illustration of hands being washed under running water

html: Breathing gets hard, a high fever won't come down, or you start to improve and then suddenly feel worse. Babies, older adults and people with lung conditions should check in sooner.
